_doc: Revert-verify mutants for RFC 14217015 P1.4 (vault-exodev task db59bc95, req 8a0ed10b): PropertyHierarchyResolvingStore widens a constant exocortex-ontology predicate to its transitive exo__Property_superProperty sub-properties. Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct sets). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › SPn @req` (ITRV §A44/§A104). `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145). Guards without a mutant: `if (!(term instanceof IRI)) return null;` and the `instanceof Literal/BlankNode` branches of termKey are type narrowing (a non-IRI declaration end cannot be a predicate; a blank or quoted object never occurs in these fixtures).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/PropertyHierarchyResolvingStore.ts

M1_no_widening._note: The decorator finds the sub-properties but never widens: the pre-fix behaviour, CQ6 returns 1 of 4. Type-preserving form (`length < 0`, never true): `&& false` drops the narrowing of `subProperties` and breaks compilation (ITRV §A36).

M2_closure_not_transitive._note: Only DIRECT sub-properties are seen; a sub-sub-property (youtubeVideo ⊑ video ⊑ exoizable) is lost.

M3_no_dedup._note: A value reached through the property and a sub-property (or two sub-properties) comes back twice.

M4_no_namespace_gate._note: The W3C vocabulary is widened too: the live declaration exo__Statement_object ⊑ rdf__subject puts statement objects into rdf:subject.

M5_instance_class_widened._note: exo:Instance_class is widened by its declared sub-properties — class membership through an arbitrary property.

M6_superclass_widened._note: exo:Class_superClass is widened by its declared sub-properties — the class walk owned by ClassHierarchyResolvingStore changes.

M7_file_iri_end_unresolved._note: A FILE-IRI declaration end is not turned into its predicate form: every frontmatter declaration is lost; only the reified-Statement one (both ends symbolic, SP14) survives.

M8_symbolic_end_dropped._note: A SYMBOLIC declaration end is dropped: every bare-UID declaration (symbolic parent) and the reified-Statement one (symbolic child) are lost; only the label-form one (both ends file IRIs, SP6) survives.

M9_index_never_invalidated._note: The index outlives a store change: a declaration added after the first query is never seen.

M10_cached_array_mutated._note: The rewritten sub-property triples are pushed into the in-memory store's CACHED result array, so a later raw match returns them as stored triples.
M10_cached_array_mutated.to: const out = await this.real.match(subject, predicate, object);

M11_property_in_own_closure._note: A property becomes its own sub-property (self-declaration, cycle): the direct match runs twice; the dedup hides it in the rows, the match count does not.

M12_predicate_not_rewritten._note: Sub-property triples come back with their stored predicate instead of the entailed one; invisible to SPARQL bindings (the dedup ignores the predicate), visible on the decorator contract.

M13_human_label_taken_as_predicate._note: A human (literal) label is taken as a predicate IRI: the IRI constructor rejects it and the whole query fails.
M13_human_label_taken_as_predicate.to: if (label.object instanceof IRI || label.object instanceof Literal) return label.object.value;

M14_exact_predicate_widened._note: matchExactPredicate widens like match: a predicate bound from a variable is widened, so the result depends on pattern order (review H1) and queryOwn through a label-bound ?p reaches inherited sub-property values and labels them own (review M1).

M15_xsd_string_not_normalized._note: A simple literal and the same xsd:string literal reached through two properties come back as two values (review L2).

M16_diamond_descendant_revisited._note: A descendant reached through two declaration paths enters the closure twice; the dedup hides it in the rows, the match count does not (review L5). Type-preserving form (`length < 0`, never true). Also SP15: the same check is what keeps the PARENT out of its own closure (`visited` starts with it) — without it a self-declaration P ⊑ P puts P into its closure and the direct match runs twice. M11 removes the other half (the parent's seed in `visited`) and reddens SP15 alone.

MX1_widen_upward._note: Declarations read backwards (contributed by the review): a query by a sub-property sees its parent (SP3), a query by the parent sees nothing extra (every widening axis). SP5 stays green — a cycle is symmetric under the swap.
MX1_widen_upward.from:
const child = await this.toPredicateForm(d.subject);
      const parent = await this.toPredicateForm(d.object);
MX1_widen_upward.to:
const child = await this.toPredicateForm(d.object);
      const parent = await this.toPredicateForm(d.subject);

MX2_unbound_variable_predicate_widened._note: An UNBOUND variable predicate gets entailed triples added (contributed by the review): `?s ?p ?o` returns the stored predicate AND its parents (SP11), and the bind-last join of SP20 sees them through the later label pattern.
